output.summary: Spindle wear (H3) is the best-supported driver: runout rose on all six Line 3 lathes (2-3 um in May to 4-11 um in October), L3-02 vibration climbed steadily, and the spindle service was deferred twice for backlog. The fatigue (H1) and new-operator (H4) claims are weak or contradicted: tag timing is batch-written at shift end, and new and experienced operators reject at similar rates. Hardness (H2) is confounded with spindle drift and unresolved. The customer-side reject rise supports a real defect increase (H5). Complete the overdue spindle service with staggered Tamsworth/Corvane trials, and pull Line 6 CMM results and hour-of-machining data before committing further. Do not cut CMM sampling, penalize operators, or report the 8-hour return as the root cause. Diagnosis is insufficient for a substantive commitment.
